records.deidentified_narrative: on [date] at approximately 1236 hours, police responded to parking lot #8 at palo alto college regarding a report of a vehicle collision. dispatch advised that no parties were injured and no one was requesting ems. upon arrival, i made contact with both involved parties. both confirmed that they were not injured and declined medical attention. the driver of unit #1, identified as ashley pimentel, stated she was attempting to park in a space next to unit #2, which was already parked and backed into a parking space. while maneuvering her vehicle, pimentel struck unit #2 with the passenger side of her vehicle, causing visible damage to both units. pimentel stated that unit #1 belongs to her mother. i then spoke with dorian vidal, who witnessed the accident. vidal stated that unit #2 belongs [school facility] earlier in the day. vidal explained that he was returning from class when he witnessed unit #1 strike unit #2. he confirmed that he was not inside unit #2 at the time of the collision and only observed the incident. upon inspection, i noted the following:unit #1: impact damage along the passenger-side front and rear doors. unit #2: scrapes and paint transfer consistent with contact from unit #1. both vehicles were observed to be in their original positions and had not been moved prior to my arrival. both parties exchanged information and were provided with a [case id] for their records. my body-worn camera (bwc) was active during this incident. end of report

unable to begin recording immediately. once the scene was safe and stabilized, i successfully began recording. the major accident involved three primary individuals. the driver of the vehicle was identified through her texas drivers license number 24336641 as unit 1, w/f dob february 21, 1990. the vehicle she was operating was a gray 2011 mazda 3 bearing texas license plate [identifier], vin 3mzbm1k76gm293274. unit 3 stated [school facility] that morning. they were crossing at the crosswalk located at the [roadway], [school facility]. unit 3 reported that as they entered the crosswalk, he observed a gray vehicle approaching from the west at what appeared to be a high rate of speed. he said the driver attempted to brake, causing the tires to screech, but was unable to stop before striking unit 2. unit 3 explained that the impact caused him to be hit as well, resulting in pain in his leg. he further stated that after the collision, he carried unit 2 back to their residence, where the childs mother was located. lakendra reported that when unit 3 brought unit 2 inside, the child was bleeding profusely from the mouth. she also stated that she did not witness the crash herself, as she had been inside the house at the time. unit 3 confirmed that both he and unit 2 had been fully within the crosswalk when they were struck. i then conducted an interview with the driver, unit 1. unit 1 stated that she had been [roadway] and had stopped at the stop sign near the [roadway]. she explained that while she was stopped at the sign, she noticed the pedestrians nearby, but said that it appeared to her they did not intend to cross. unit 1 stated that she began making her turn and was surprised when the pedestrians entered the crosswalk. she said she immediately attempted to brake, and although she heard her tires screech, she was unable to stop in time, resulting in the collision. unit 1 initially maintained that the pedestrians had not yet entered the crosswalk, but after i informed her that blood evidence was located inside the crosswalk, she admitted that the collision had in fact occurred there. there were initially conflicting accounts regarding the pedestrians location at the time of the collision. unit 3 consistently stated that they were within the crosswalk, while unit 1 originally claimed they were still on the sidewalk and appeared not to be crossing. after being presented with the physical evidence, unit 1 acknowledged that the pedestrians were already in the crosswalk when she turned and struck them. i documented the scene with photographs, including evidence of blood approximately fifteen feet north of where the crosswalk begins on the south side of the roadway. visible injuries were noted on both victims: unit 2 sustained bleeding from the mouth, and unit 3 reported pain in his right leg consistent with the impact of unit 2 being struck in his right leg. based on the statements of the victims, the drivers admission, and the physical evidence collected at the scene, i determined that the driver failed to yield the right of way to pedestrians within a crosswalk. this constitutes a violation under texas transportation code § 545. 428, motor vehicle collision [roadway] user within area of crosswalk. the statute states that a person commits an offense if, with criminal negligence, they operate a motor records.public_safe_text: on october 24, 2024, i, officer ortiz, was dispatched to a major accident at the [roadway] at approximately 0751 hours. the call text stated that a child had been struck by a vehicle and was bleeding from the mouth. upon arrival at the scene, i attempted to activate my body-worn camera; however, due to a connection issue between my remote and the device, i was unable to begin recording immediately. once the scene was safe and stabilized, i successfully began recording. the major accident involved three primary individuals. the driver of the vehicle was identified through her texas drivers license number 24336641 as unit 1, w/f dob february 21, 1990. the vehicle she was operating was a gray 2011 mazda 3 bearing texas license plate [identifier], vin 3mzbm1k76gm293274. unit 3 stated [school facility] that morning. they were crossing at the crosswalk located at the [roadway], [school facility]. unit 3 reported that as they entered the crosswalk, he observed a gray vehicle approaching from the west at what appeared to be a high rate of speed. he said the driver attempted to brake, causing the tires to screech, but was unable to stop before striking unit 2. unit 3 explained that the impact caused him to be hit as well, resulting in pain in his leg. he further stated that after the collision, he carried unit 2 back to their residence, where the childs mother was located. lakendra reported that when unit 3 brought unit 2 inside, the child was bleeding profusely from the mouth. she also stated that she did not witness the crash herself, as she had been inside the house at the time. unit 3 confirmed that both he and unit 2 had been fully within the crosswalk when they were struck. i then conducted an interview with the driver, unit 1. unit 1 stated that she had been [roadway] and had stopped at the stop sign near the [roadway]. she explained that while she was stopped at the sign, she noticed the pedestrians nearby, but said that it appeared to her they did not intend to cross. unit 1 stated that she began making her turn and was surprised when the pedestrians entered the crosswalk. she said she immediately attempted to brake, and although she heard her tires screech, she was unable to stop in time, resulting in the collision. unit 1 initially maintained that the pedestrians had not yet entered the crosswalk, but after i informed her that blood evidence was located inside the crosswalk, she admitted that the collision had in fact occurred there. there were initially conflicting accounts regarding the pedestrians location at the time of the collision. unit 3 consistently stated that they were within the crosswalk, while unit 1 originally claimed they were still on the sidewalk and appeared not to be crossing. after being presented with the physical evidence, unit 1 acknowledged that the pedestrians were already in the crosswalk when she turned and struck them. i documented the scene with photographs, including evidence of blood approximately fifteen feet north of where the crosswalk begins on the south side of the roadway. visible injuries were noted on both victims: unit 2 sustained bleeding from the mouth, and unit 3 reported pain in his right leg consistent with the impact of unit 2 being struck in his right leg. based on the statements of the victims, the drivers admission, and the physical evidence collected at the scene, i determined that the driver failed to yield the right of way to pedestrians within a crosswalk. this constitutes a violation under texas transportation code § 545. 428, motor vehicle collision [roadway] user within area of crosswalk. the statute states that a person commits an offense if, with criminal negligence, they operate a motor vehicle within the area of a crosswalk and cause bodily injury to [roadway] user. this offense is classified as a class a misdemeanor. i am charging unit 1 with only one count of this offense, due to unit 3 not having visible bodily injury to his leg, refusing medical treatment, [medical facility]. i provided the childs mother, lakendra kendrix, with a yellow copy of the crash report and the insurance information belonging to unit 1. unit 1 was advised of the charges and informed that the case would be forwarded to a detective for further review. she acknowledged and left the scene without further incident. unit 2 was transported [medical facility] at [roadway], fort worth, texas, for further evaluation. paramedics reported that he sustained suspected injuries, which were not life-threatening. although nothing appeared to be broken or serious, [medical facility] for further medical assessment. i also completed a cr-3 with the information gathered; reference 2 reported injuries under this [case id]. there is nothing further to report at this time. officer c. ortiz #3718south patrol district

records.deidentified_narrative: police responded to a call for a pedestrian that was struck by vehicle. i arrived on scene and made contact with the pedestrian struck by unit 1. pedestrian stated she got out of her vehicle to use the restroom at the park. pedestrian stated that her vehicle was parked next to unit 1 when he started backing out of the parking spot. pedestrian stated that unit 1 started turning to exit the parking lot trapping her in between the front right bumper of unit 1 and her vehicle. pedestrian stated that unit 1 continued to back up pinning her and injuring her. pedestrian stated that unit 1 finally stopped when her mother started hitting the car telling the driver of unit 1 to stop. i then spoke with driver of unit 1 who stated that he saw the pedestrian exit her vehicle. driver of unit 1 stated that he started to back up and started turning to avoid hitting the poles behind him. driver of unit 1 stated he did not see the pedestrian and stopped because the mother of the pedestrian started hitting his window and vehicle. the area where the accident occurred had no lighting. driver of unit 1 stated that the pedestrians mother started threatening him saying they will ""drag him out of the car and beat him"". driver of unit 1 did not show any signs of being under the influence. driver of unit 1 asked to have sfst's conducted on him to calm the pedestrians family. officer sanchez #1853 conducted sfst's on driver of unit 1. no clues of intoxication were found. pedestrian was transported by ems unit#[medical facility] for her injuries. in my opinion, driver of unit 1 was at fault for the accident for not checking the area was clear and safe prior to exiting the parking spot.

records.public_safe_text: on november 8, 2025 at about 0242 hours, desoto traffic ofc. v. gonzalez #298 was contacted by desoto traffic cpl. quick #[roadway] with entrapment in the area of southbound 1400 block of n i35e, desoto, dallas county, texas. this is a secondary crash. please see original crash under report number 2025-00511553 upon arrival, ofc. v. gonzalez observed four wrecked vehicles. a white chevrolet express 2500 van with tx lp [identifier] (unit 1). unit 1 was resting on its roof, [roadway] 3 and 4, facing east with heavy damage all over. a dark gray dodge challenger with tx lp [identifier] (unit 2). unit 2 [roadway] 3 (about 150 ft south of unit 1), facing west with heavy damage to its front end and moderate damage to its right/passenger side. a blue kia k4 with tx lp [identifier] (unit). unit 3 was resting in the left shoulder, facing southeast, with heavy damage to its front end. and a black ford explorer with tx lp [identifier] (unit 4), which was sitting on the right shoulder, facing south, with moderate damage to its front end/right side. ofc. v. gonzalez was briefed by responding officers of the facts. here is a summary of what occurred: unit 1 was involved in a single vehicle collision as it was traveling southbound on i35e. unit 1 struck, with its front end/right side, the crash barrels [roadway] exit ramp (415). the impact caused unit 1 to roll on its left/driver side [roadway] 3 and 4 facing east. the operator of unit 1 (unit 5) managed to climb out of unit 1 via passenger side, [roadway] and landed right next to unit 1 where unit 5 remained (standing). unit 2 approached the collision and swerved to left in an attempt to [person] 1 but still sideswiped the front end of unit 1 with its right side and then struck unit 5 who was still standing in the lanes of traffic (lane 3). unit 5, after being struck by unit 2, landed on the front windshield/right side of unit 2 and then was dragged for about 50 [roadway]/the lanes of traffic (lane 3). unit 2, after sideswiping unit 1 and striking unit 5, lost control, as it continued traveling southbound, and then struck, with its front end, the west side retaining wall where it bounced off [roadway] 3. unit 3 approached the collision as [roadway] 3. unit 3 struck, with its front end, the center of the roof of unit 1. the impact caused unit 1 to flip on its roof and unit 3 to be propelled to the east nearly colliding with the center barrier before coming to rest. finally, unit 4 approached the collision, managed to avoid unit 1 and unit 3 but sideswiped, with its front end/right side, the rear end/right side of unit 2 which caused unit 4 to lose control and strike the west side retaining wall. dallas county district attorney's office investigator sgt. cathcart used his 3d scanner to scan the entire crash scene. dallas county district attorney's office investigator sgt. cathcart will provide desoto traffic unit with a copy of the scan. the operator of unit 1 was pronounced deceased on scene at 0239 hours by desoto fire engine 261. all four occupants from unit 3 were transported by desoto [medical facility]. louise bradshaw and latonya bogney (passenger of unit 3) were both listed in critical condition. the occupants of unit 4 and the [medical facility]. all units were impounded. on december 4, 2025, desoto traffic ofc. v. gonzalez #298 updated this case with the following information:bogney, latonya succumbed to her injuries on november 26, 2025, at [roadway]. calista ejim. medical examiner office was also updated with this information (me reference # 25-19053). this case will be closed.
